category: premium file host (one-click hoster), retrieval target

free_tier.stated: No free allowance is published on the premium page; the page sells only the paid tier ('30Days 20.00 USD ... 100 GB daily traffic'). Free-mode behaviour is known only from a third-party measurement: 30.0 KB/s in Chrome.

per_object_cap.stated: not established for the free tier; the premium page sells speed, not size

retention.stated: not established; the premium page states no retention window

egress.terms: Premium is sold as '100 GB daily traffic' with 'Max download speed', 'Parallel downloads' and 'No waiting time'. Traffic is metered by design and the daily allowance is the product.
egress.free_allowance: 100 GB/day on every premium plan (93.13 GiB/day, 2.73 TiB/30d)
egress.price_per_tb: no overage price published; the next plan up is the only way to buy more

interface_detail: No public API documentation was found on the site. JDownloader 2 works against it per the 2026 third-party test.
tooling: JDownloader 2 (37.8 MB/s combined in the July 2026 test); browser premium 14.4 MB/s
chaining: A 100 GB/day key covers one TiB a month with 2.7x headroom, so it composes as a paid fallback when a link is UploadGIG-only and no debrid covers it.

limits.value: free tier measured at 30.0 KB/s = 0.0286 MiB/s

limits_note: The vendor publishes no free-tier number at all; the only free figure is a third-party browser measurement.
binding_note: At 1 TiB/month the 100 GB/day allowance is 2.7x the requirement, so the first thing to fail is the daily counter only if the client bursts; otherwise the price does.

identity_cost.detail: Account is an e-mail signup. Payment is by card or crypto through the vendor's payment page; no phone or identity document is asked for.

reliability_note: Free mode is throttled to roughly 30 KB/s and carries waiting and ads; premium removes both. Upload fails are retried by JDownloader 2 without special handling.
confidence_note: Price and daily allowance are from the vendor premium page read. The free-tier speed is third-party. A paid download through the vendor API would raise it to measured.

evidence.proved: USD 20.00/30 days, 50.00/90, 80.00/180, 140.00/365, '100 GB daily traffic', 'Max download speed', 'Parallel downloads', 'No waiting time'
third-party July 2026 test: JD2 37.8 MB/s combined, browser premium 14.4 MB/s, free 30.0 KB/s

price_per_tb_month: USD 7.33 per TiB-month at the 30-day plan (USD 20.00 for 2.73 TiB of allowance), USD 4.22 at 365 days
notes: Kept as the cheapest per-TiB host in the 30-day bracket that is not a video host. Its weakness is coverage, not price: the 2026 test ranks it 9th of 12 and calls it a budget pick.

extras.price_ladder_reported: USD 20.00 / 30 days; USD 50.00 / 90 days; USD 80.00 / 180 days; USD 140.00 / 365 days
